# Cutting evaluation protocol

This protocol validates measured behavior, not a guarantee of a proof count.
Synthetic unit tests establish contracts; they do not establish real-world precision.

## Sources and annotation

Use generated or explicitly authorized public media in repository fixtures. Keep private
footage, the historical bishop case inventory and annotations under its external edit
directory. Record source fingerprints, rights/consent, recording language, microphones,
channels, synchronization, model/tool identities and the frozen policy hash.

Partition entire source programs into calibration and held-out sets before tuning.
Do not share an occurrence or alternate take between splits. Freeze profile parameters,
eligibility and analysis/runtime settings before held-out execution. A failed held-out
assessment requires a new version and an untouched subsequent evaluation set.

Two independent annotators inspect original audiovisual context, complete attempts and
actual candidate joins. Record acceptable dispositions and boundaries, protected words,
qualification, intent, safe/unambiguous status and uncertainty. Adjudicate disagreements
without seeing model confidence. Unknown cases stay unknown; historical preview approval
alone does not certify acoustic boundaries.

## Coverage and outcomes

Validate PT-BR and English separately. Represent all six formats and three intensities
in each language, with preservation negatives as well as cleanable pauses/retakes.
Report counts and uncertainty by category/profile; sparse or untested strata remain
unvalidated. Include quiet/unvoiced speech, omitted syllables, intentional repetition,
numbers/negatives/names, unclear delivery, overlapping speech, meaningful holds and tiny
legitimate events. Include all 25 historical reports externally with honest dispositions.

Aggregate claims require at least 200 automatic decisions and 200 independently
annotated safe/unambiguous cases per language. Precision is accepted automatic decisions
divided by **all** automatic decisions, including wrong and unsafe edits. Safe resolution
is accepted automatically resolved safe cases divided by all annotated safe cases.
Require >=98% precision, >=80% safe resolution and zero severe protection violations.
Report Wilson 95% binomial intervals; point targets and intervals are distinct.

Compare avoidable technical correction requests after the first complete proof on the
same approved editorial brief. Prefer at least three paired programs per language;
report >=50% reduction only when the denominator and completed reviews exist. Damaged
words, unwanted residue, accidental duplication, unsafe replacements and confirmed
dispensable pauses are technical corrections. Creative preferences and substantive
shortening requests have separate counts. A baseline of zero produces an undefined
reduction, not an invented success.

## Reporting

Save immutable measured results in an external evaluation directory, with a nonprivate
summary in the feature documentation. Missing measurements are null. Failed/missing
models, uninspected joins and unresolved selection changes are not passes. Distinguish
automatic checks, inferred model observations and actual human listening/viewing.
An insufficient benchmark blocks the validation claim; it does not justify lowering
thresholds, relabeling historical uncertainty or fabricating media/annotations.
